record.title: Saint Sebastian
record.scan_source: Photogrammetric scan of the painted and gilded wooden sculpture.
record.scan_author: Cleveland Museum of Art / Dale Utt
record.note: The adult martyr twists against the tree to which he is bound. This German devotional carving brings together a flowing pose and sharply cut hair and drapery. Saint Sebastian later became a recurring figure in homoerotic art and queer reception; that later reading is distinct from this work’s original religious purpose.

record.title: Hercules Wrestling with Antaeus
record.museum: SMK – National Gallery of Denmark, Copenhagen
record.source_institution: SMK – National Gallery of Denmark, Copenhagen
record.scan_source: Photogrammetric scan of the alabaster sculpture and its base.
record.note: Hercules lifts Antaeus from the earth, the source of the giant’s strength. Their interlocked bodies give the combat a striking physical intimacy. Renaissance statuettes of this subject have a documented history as signifiers of same-sex attraction; this is a contextual reading, rather than proof of this particular maker’s intention.
record.attribution: Hercules Wrestling with Antaeus. Artwork: Unknown Netherlandish artist. 3D model: Geoffrey Marchal; CC BY 4.0. Atrium derivative: geometry optimized for browser display. Exact model archived under CC BY 4.0 in Objaverse; the current Sketchfab listing carries different terms.

context.evidence: The V&A identifies Renaissance collector statuettes of Hercules, including its Hercules and Antaeus, as historical signifiers of same-sex attraction. This SMK alabaster is a different version of the same adult wrestling subject; label the connection as a contextual reading, not exact-work proven intention.

record.title: Bearded Captive (SMK cast)
record.artist: Michelangelo Buonarroti; plaster cast after the original
record.museum: SMK – National Gallery of Denmark, Royal Cast Collection
record.geography: Italy; cast in Florence for SMK, Denmark
record.source_institution: SMK – National Gallery of Denmark, Royal Cast Collection
record.scan_source: 3D scan of SMK’s 2002 plaster cast after the marble original; untextured geometry, displayed with a neutral plaster material.
record.note: A mature male figure twists within an unfinished block. The tension between the emerging body and rough stone has invited readings of confinement, desire and release, including queer art-historical readings of Michelangelo’s Captives. This scan records SMK’s plaster cast; it does not record the marble original directly.

context.evidence: Art historian Bryan C. Keene proposes a queer perspective on Michelangelo’s illustrated Captives series. Series-level queer reception, not an asserted portrait of a lover.

exhibition_placements.caption: Painted skin and gilded drapery make the martyr’s body vivid against the branching tree. This was a devotional image; its later queer reception is a separate chapter in how Saint Sebastian has been viewed.
Hercules must hold Antaeus clear of the earth to defeat him. Turning the group reveals the grips and counterweights that keep two struggling bodies suspended above a small base.
The torso emerges from rough, unfinished stone. SMK’s plaster cast preserves that contrast in relief, allowing the viewer to trace the transition between worked anatomy and the surrounding block.
